verses.zh: 以色列人在当灭的物上犯了罪；因为犹大支派中，谢拉的曾孙，撒底的孙子，迦米的儿子亚干取了当灭的物；耶和华的怒气就向以色列人发作。
verses.en: But the Israelites disobeyed the command about the city’s riches.[NOTE:1] Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi,[NOTE:2] son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, stole some of the riches.[NOTE:3] The Lord was furious with the Israelites.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “But the sons of Israel were unfaithful with unfaithfulness concerning what was set apart [to the Lord].”
1 Chr 2:6 lists a “Zimri” (but no Zabdi) as one of the five sons of Zerah (cf. also Josh 7:17, 18).
Heb “took from what was set apart [to the Lord].”

Heb “the anger of the Lord burned against the sons of Israel.”sn This incident illustrates well the principle of corporate solidarity and corporate guilt. The sin of one man brought the Lord’s anger down upon the entire nation.

verses.zh: 当下，约书亚从耶利哥打发人往伯特利东边、靠近伯・亚文的艾城去，吩咐他们说：「你们上去窥探那地。」他们就上去窥探艾城。
verses.en: Joshua sent men from Jericho[NOTE:1] to Ai (which is located near Beth Aven, east of Bethel[NOTE:2]) and instructed them, “Go up and spy on the land.” So the men went up and spied on Ai.
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
For the location of Bethel see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

verses.zh: 他们回到约书亚那里，对他说：「众民不必都上去，只要二三千人上去就能攻取艾城；不必劳累众民都去，因为那里的人少。」
verses.en: They returned and reported to Joshua,[NOTE:1] “Don’t send the whole army.[NOTE:2] About two or three thousand men are adequate to defeat Ai.[NOTE:3] Don’t tire out the whole army, for Ai is small.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and they returned to Joshua and said to him.”
Heb “Don’t let all the people go up.”
Heb “Let about two thousand men or about three thousand men go up to defeat Ai.”
Heb “all the people for they are small.”

verses.zh: 于是民中约有三千人上那里去，竟在艾城人面前逃跑了。
verses.en: So about 3,000 men went up, but they fled from the men of Ai.

verses.zh: 艾城的人击杀了他们三十六人，从城门前追赶他们，直到示巴琳，在下坡杀败他们；众民的心就消化如水。
verses.en: The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them and chased them from in front of the city gate all the way to the fissures[NOTE:1] and defeated them on the steep slope.[NOTE:2] The people’s[NOTE:3] courage melted away like water.[NOTE:4]
notes: The meaning and correct translation of the Hebrew word שְׁבָרִים (shevarim) is uncertain. The translation “fissures” is based on usage of the plural form of the noun in Ps 60:4 HT (60:2 ET), where it appears to refer to cracks in the earth caused by an earthquake. Perhaps deep ravines or gorges are in view, or the word is a proper noun (“all the way to Shebarim”).
The precise geographical location of the Israelite defeat at this “steep slope” is uncertain.
Or “army’s.”
Heb “and the heart of the people melted and became water.”

verses.zh: 约书亚便撕裂衣服；他和以色列的长老把灰撒在头上，在耶和华的约柜前俯伏在地，直到晚上。
verses.en: Joshua tore his clothes;[NOTE:1] he and the leaders[NOTE:2] of Israel lay face down on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening[NOTE:3] and threw dirt on their heads.[NOTE:4]
notes: Tearing one’s clothes was an outward expression of extreme sorrow (see Gen 37:34; 44:13).
Or “elders.”
Heb “and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel.”
Throwing dirt on one’s head was an outward expression of extreme sorrow (see Lam 2:10; Ezek 27:30).

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「哀哉！主耶和华啊，你为甚么竟领这百姓过约旦河，将我们交在亚摩利人的手中，使我们灭亡呢？我们不如住在约旦河那边倒好。
verses.en: Joshua prayed,[NOTE:1] “O, Sovereign Lord! Why did you bring these people across the Jordan to hand us over to the Amorites so they could destroy us? If only we had been satisfied to live on the other side of the Jordan!
notes: Heb “said.”

verses.zh: 主啊，以色列人既在仇敌面前转背逃跑，我还有甚么可说的呢？
verses.en: O Lord, what can I say now that Israel has retreated[NOTE:1] before its enemies?
notes: Heb “turned [the] back.”

verses.zh: 迦南人和这地一切的居民听见了就必围困我们，将我们的名从地上除灭。那时你为你的大名要怎样行呢？」
verses.en: When the Canaanites and all who live in the land hear about this, they will turn against us and destroy the very memory of us[NOTE:1] from the earth. What will you do to protect your great reputation?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and cut off our name.”
Heb “What will you do for your great name?”

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐约书亚说：「起来！你为何这样俯伏在地呢？
verses.en: The Lord responded[NOTE:1] to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying there face down?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “said.”
Heb “Why are you falling on your face?”

verses.zh: 以色列人犯了罪，违背了我所吩咐他们的约，取了当灭的物；又偷窃，又行诡诈，又把那当灭的放在他们的家具里。
verses.en: Israel has sinned; they have violated my covenantal commandment![NOTE:1] They have taken some of the riches;[NOTE:2] they have stolen them and deceitfully put them among their own possessions.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “They have violated my covenant which I commanded them.”
Heb “what was set apart [to the Lord].”
Heb “and also they have stolen, and also they have lied, and also they have placed [them] among their items.”

verses.zh: 因此，以色列人在仇敌面前站立不住。他们在仇敌面前转背逃跑，是因成了被咒诅的；你们若不把当灭的物从你们中间除掉，我就不再与你们同在了。
verses.en: The Israelites are unable to stand before their enemies; they retreat because they have become subject to annihilation.[NOTE:1] I will no longer be with you,[NOTE:2] unless you destroy what has contaminated you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they turn [the] back before their enemies because they are set apart [to destruction by the Lord].”
The second person pronoun is plural in Hebrew, indicating these words are addressed to the entire nation.
Heb “what is set apart [to destruction by the Lord] from your midst.”

verses.zh: 你起来，叫百姓自洁，对他们说：『你们要自洁，预备明天，因为耶和华―以色列的　神这样说：以色列啊，你们中间有当灭的物，你们若不除掉，在仇敌面前必站立不住！』
verses.en: Get up! Ritually consecrate the people and tell them this: ‘Ritually consecrate yourselves for tomorrow because this is what the Lord God of Israel has said, “You are contaminated,[NOTE:1] O Israel! You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove what is contaminating you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “what is set apart [to destruction by the Lord] [is] in your midst.”
Heb “remove what is set apart [i.e., to destruction by the Lord] from your midst.”

verses.zh: 到了早晨，你们要按着支派近前来；耶和华所取的支派，要按着宗族近前来；耶和华所取的宗族，要按着家室近前来；耶和华所取的家室，要按着人丁，一个一个地近前来。
verses.en: In the morning you must approach in tribal order.[NOTE:1] The tribe the Lord selects[NOTE:2] must approach by clans. The clan the Lord selects must approach by families.[NOTE:3] The family the Lord selects must approach man by man.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “by your tribes.”
Heb “takes forcefully, seizes.”
Heb “houses.”
Heb “by men.”

verses.zh: 被取的人有当灭的物在他那里，他和他所有的必被火焚烧；因他违背了耶和华的约，又因他在以色列中行了愚妄的事。」
verses.en: The one caught with the riches[NOTE:1] must be burned up[NOTE:2] along with all who belong to him because he violated the Lord’s covenant and did such a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”
notes: Heb “with what was set apart [to the Lord].”
Heb “burned with fire.”

verses.zh: 于是，约书亚清早起来，使以色列人按着支派近前来，取出来的是犹大支派；
verses.en: Bright and early the next morning Joshua made Israel approach in tribal order,[NOTE:1] and the tribe of Judah was selected.
notes: Heb “by tribes.”

verses.zh: 使犹大支派（原文是宗族）近前来，就取了谢拉的宗族；使谢拉的宗族，按着家室人丁，一个一个地近前来，取出来的是撒底；
verses.en: He then made the clans of Judah approach, and the clan of the Zerahites was selected. He made the clan of the Zerahites approach, and Zabdi[NOTE:1] was selected.[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on “Zabdi” in Jos 7:1.
Heb “and he selected Zabdi.” The Lord is the apparent subject. The LXX supports reading a passive (Niphal) form here, as does the immediate context.

verses.zh: 使撒底的家室，按着人丁，一个一个地近前来，就取出犹大支派的人谢拉的曾孙，撒底的孙子，迦米的儿子亚干。
verses.en: He then made Zabdi’s[NOTE:1] family approach man by man[NOTE:2] and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was selected.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Zabdi) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “by men.”

verses.zh: 约书亚对亚干说：「我儿，我劝你将荣耀归给耶和华―以色列的　神，在他面前认罪，将你所做的事告诉我，不要向我隐瞒。」
verses.en: So Joshua said to Achan, “My son, honor[NOTE:1] the Lord God of Israel and give him praise! Tell me what you did; don’t hide anything from me.”
notes: Heb “give glory to.”

verses.zh: 亚干回答约书亚说：「我实在得罪了耶和华―以色列的　神。我所做的事如此如此：
verses.en: Achan told Joshua, “It is true. I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel in this way:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “like this and like this I did.”

verses.zh: 我在所夺的财物中看见一件美好的示拿衣服，二百舍客勒银子，一条金子重五十舍客勒，我就贪爱这些物件，便拿去了。现今藏在我帐棚内的地里，银子在衣服底下。」
verses.en: I saw among the goods we seized a nice robe from Babylon,[NOTE:1] 200 silver pieces,[NOTE:2] and a bar of gold weighing 50 shekels. I wanted them, so I took them. They are hidden in the ground right in the middle of my tent, with the silver underneath.”
notes: Heb “Shinar,” a reference to Babylon (cf. Gen 10:10; 11:2; 14:1). Many modern translations retain the Hebrew name “Shinar” (cf. NEB, NRSV) but some use the more familiar “Babylon” (cf. NIV, NLT).
Heb “shekels.”

verses.zh: 约书亚就打发人跑到亚干的帐棚里。那件衣服果然藏在他帐棚内，银子在底下。
verses.en: Joshua sent messengers who ran to the tent. The things were hidden right in his tent, with the silver underneath.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Look, [it was] hidden in his tent, and the silver was beneath it.”

verses.zh: 他们就从帐棚里取出来，拿到约书亚和以色列众人那里，放在耶和华面前。
verses.en: They took it all from the middle of the tent, brought it to Joshua and all the Israelites, and placed[NOTE:1] it before the Lord.
notes: Heb “poured out,” probably referring to the way the silver pieces poured out of their container.

verses.zh: 约书亚和以色列众人把谢拉的曾孙亚干和那银子、那件衣服、那条金子，并亚干的儿女、牛、驴、羊、帐棚，以及他所有的，都带到亚割谷去。
verses.en: Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan, son of Zerah, along with the silver, the robe, the bar of gold, his sons, daughters, oxen, donkeys, sheep, tent, and all that belonged to him and brought them up to the Valley of Disaster.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “Trouble” The name is “Achor” in Hebrew, which means “disaster” or “trouble” (also in v. 26).

verses.zh: 约书亚说：「你为甚么连累我们呢？今日耶和华必叫你受连累。」于是以色列众人用石头打死他，将石头扔在其上，又用火焚烧他所有的（原文是他们）。
verses.en: Joshua said, “Why have you brought disaster on[NOTE:1] us? The Lord will bring disaster on you today!” All Israel stoned him to death. (They also stoned and burned the others.)[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “trouble on.” The word is “achor” in Hebrew (also in the following clause).
Heb “and they burned them with fire and they stoned them with stones.” These words are somewhat parenthetical in nature and are omitted in the LXX; they may represent a later scribal addition.

verses.zh: 众人在亚干身上堆成一大堆石头，直存到今日。于是耶和华转意，不发他的烈怒。因此那地方名叫亚割谷（就是连累的意思），直到今日。
verses.en: Then they erected over him a large pile of stones (it remains to this very day[NOTE:1]), and the Lord’s anger subsided. So that place is called the Valley of Disaster to this very day.
notes: Heb “to this day.” The phrase “to this day” is omitted in the LXX and may represent a later scribal addition.
